Can China Export Its Nuclear Boom?

AJ Cortese

Gavekal Technologies: New Energy | 12 Oct 2026

China is the world’s biggest builder of nuclear power plants, but unlike in other energy sectors it has not become a significant exporter of reactors. The international market is still dominated by Russia, with South Korea beginning to pick up some projects in the Middle East and Europe with its low-cost models. So far China’s only overseas projects are in Pakistan, a close strategic ally. For the moment Chinese nuclear firms have their hands full satisfying domestic demand. And while they have figured out how to make reactors relatively cheaply, the complexity and safety needs of nuclear projects mean they will never be able to gobble up world markets through ultralow prices, as Chinese solar, EV and battery firms have done. But over the next decade it is likely China will become an important nuclear exporter, thanks to its ability to combine low cost, quick construction time, and state-backed financing support.Also in this issue of New Energy Insight:
